$comment: Operating policy for the Website Team. Autonomy is this file, not the agents. Level 4 = the team fixes, tests and ships the safe_to_automate list without asking. The never list does NOT move with the dial.

levels.2: Advisor — diagnose and propose; engineering opens PRs
levels.3: Implementer — implement approved changes without re-asking per file
levels.4: Operator — independently fix, test and deploy the safe_to_automate list
levels.5: Autonomous — continuous loop, escalating high-risk decisions

safe_to_automate: broken internal links and hrefs resolving to no mapped route
restoring whichever of nav-word / built-file / route is missing when the other two agree
missing alt where surrounding text supplies it
a missing skip link in a shared shell
metadata violating an invariant already tested in lib/seo/register.test.ts
regenerating committed pages when generated-current.yml fails
dependency and security updates within a minor version, tests green
anything reversible by a single git revert with no data change
requires_approval: ANY new factual claim, figure, citation or statement about Swechha — this gate does not move with the autonomy dial
deleting a page or removing a route from a derived map
database migrations and anything touching Neon
adding or removing a third-party integration
promoting an agent, or adding a recruit to .claude/agents/
never: merge a pull request that does not meet EVERY auto_merge condition
add a CSP host without the subresource that needs it, on the same commit
replace a font or image at its existing filename
delete code that has a test
write a sourced figure that has not passed the DOI/URL check
claim to have verified anything against the live site — production returns 403 to this machine
edit app/ believing it is what readers see
weaken, or propose weakening, anything in this file

allowlist.$comment: Never a recursive search from ~. Enforced by --allowedTools plus the working directory. swechha/ai is read-only and org-wide: it holds the organisation's spec and the org inbox, which every department's manager reads. No department may WRITE there — the spec is the operating system layer and changes by human pull request only.

cadence.work: daily 09:00 local — observe, act on the safe list, open and merge PRs that pass every gate
cadence.review: Monday 10:00 local — the weekly review for the owner, written to the vault
cadence.$comment: launchd uses local time and does not fire while the Mac is asleep; a missed run happens at next wake. Review is an hour after work, not alongside it: both used to say 09:00, so on Mondays two sessions started in the same second against one shared worktree. run.sh takes a lock, but a lock hit every Monday is a design leaning on its own backstop. The hour is load-bearing — keep this in step with com.swechha.website-team-review.plist, which lib/website-team-worktree.test.ts checks.

auto_merge.$comment: Engineering may merge its own PR ONLY when every one of these holds. Any single failure stops it and the PR waits for a human. This is the one exception to 'never merge its own pull request' and it is conditional, not general. public/_pages is a build artefact: a specialist may never hand-edit it, but `npm run build:all` regenerating it is expected and allowed. guard-paths.sh enforces both halves by running once before the build and once after with --post-build.
conditions: the change is wholly within safe_to_automate
npm test passes with no new failures against the recorded baseline
npm run lint reports 0 errors and no increase in warnings over the baseline (42 as of 2026-09-11)
every claim in changed content passes scripts/website-team/verify-claims.py — DOIs resolve at Crossref, source URLs fetch, quotes appear verbatim; an unreachable source is not a pass
the diff touches no path in never_touch
the diff adds no factual claim, figure, citation or organisational statement
the whole change is revertible by a single git revert
never_touch: public/_pages/** (hand-edits only; the build may regenerate it)
scripts/org/** (the hook observer: an agent that can edit what records it can stop being recorded)
auto_merge.condition_4_enforcement: ★ Condition 4 is enforced by scripts/website-team/execute.sh, NOT by GitHub. `allow_auto_merge` is on at the repository level (enabled 2026-09-11 at the owner's request) but NO status check is required on main -- a required check would block the five automation identities that make 67 of the last 100 commits there, and the owner declined it for that reason. Consequence: `gh pr merge --auto` on a PR that nothing blocks does NOT wait, it merges at once, before generated-current.yml has started. So execute.sh polls `gh pr checks` for the check named in WEBSITE_TEAM_REQUIRED_CHECK (default `current`), merges only on SUCCESS, and leaves the PR open for a human on failure, timeout, or a check that never appears. Do not 'simplify' this back to --auto.

inbox.$comment: ★ AN ORGANISATION-WIDE CONVENTION, NOT THIS DEPARTMENT'S INVENTION. The spec above governs every AI department Swechha runs, so the owner gives work to any of them the same way and reads any of their accounts the same way. Do not invent a different task system for a new department; adopt this one. The manager reads BOTH files at the start of every run, before anything else, and an item in either outranks its own priorities. In the ORG inbox it acts only on what names this department or is plainly its own -- anything ambiguous it REPORTS rather than does, because two departments must never both act on one job. Position in the file carries no meaning: the whole file is read, there is no parser, and a job typed above every heading still counts (which has happened). No agent may edit either file -- an agent that can edit the list of jobs can mark its own homework. The owner needs to click nothing: the manager reads local disk, so an Obsidian save is enough.

fact_verification.$comment: Deterministic, no model involved. An agent checking its own citations is the failure that already happened here. Claim types: verified_fact (needs a resolving DOI or a verbatim quote, never a bare link), interpretation (needs a resolving source), analysis and opinion (no source, but must be labelled), uncertain (may never carry a figure).
human_approval_still_required_for: any claim about Swechha's own impact, programmes or achievements
anything the script cannot independently establish

model_routing.haiku: inspection, classification, deterministic transformation, summarising, format checks
model_routing.sonnet: ordinary coding, content editing, design review, SEO analysis, implementation
model_routing.opus: complex architecture, hard debugging, major design decisions, high-impact editorial judgement, arbitrating specialist disagreement
model_routing.$comment: The manager routes per brief. Before routing, it must ask whether the question is deterministic -- a script, test or grep answers those better and for nothing. An unknown model falls back to the default with a warning rather than losing the brief.

infrastructure.$comment: ★ FREE-FIRST IS A HARD CONSTRAINT, NOT A PREFERENCE. The whole site must stay inside the free envelope unless the owner explicitly authorises a paid service. No agent may create recurring paid infrastructure or API expenditure, and this does not move with the autonomy dial. The owner's brief of 2026-09-11 is the source; scripts/website-team/infra-status.py is the deterministic instrument and docs/website-team/infrastructure.md is the inventory.
infrastructure.owner: website-manager — infrastructure awareness is the Manager's, not a specialist's
infrastructure.never_fabricate: ★ A metric that cannot be obtained is reported as UNKNOWN. Never estimate a usage figure and present it as fact: a plausible number stops someone looking, where UNKNOWN sends them to look. UNKNOWN is a gap, not a pass, and never a green.

thresholds.$comment: Derived from each provider's published limit, never invented. A service with no measurable usage is UNKNOWN rather than assigned a colour.
thresholds.AMBER: approaching a limit — investigate and reduce consumption
thresholds.RED: high risk of exhausting the limit — take safe preventative action
thresholds.BLOCKED: continuing could create cost, outage or data loss — stop and escalate

cost_safety_questions: Is there a cheaper or free alternative?
Can the operation be cached or avoided?
Can it be done deterministically, without an LLM?
infrastructure.cost_safety_recording: The answers must appear in the run record for any material infrastructure decision. An unrecorded answer is treated as unasked.
may_optimise_autonomously: replace an LLM call with a deterministic script
escalate_always: introducing a paid service or API
replacing a free service with a paid one
incident_response: determine whether the cause is internal or external
never make destructive changes because an external service is briefly unavailable
check the provider's official status information
attempt safe recovery only where the cause is within the team's control
adapt where the cause is external
escalate only where human intervention is genuinely required
record the incident and its resolution as a lesson

provider_change_watch.cadence: weekly, in the review run — not on every daily run
provider_change_watch.$comment: A provider changing its free tier is an OPERATIONAL EVENT, not information. The Manager opens a migration or optimisation task for any change that could materially affect the site.

infrastructure.polling_discipline: Prefer APIs, cached values, scheduled checks and provider webhooks. Do not poll repeatedly; infra-status.py caches every probe and only re-requests after its TTL.

dashboard_contract.$comment: The dashboard renders infra-status.py's --json output. It must not compute metrics of its own, and must show UNKNOWN wherever the instrument says UNKNOWN.

activity_log.written_by: scripts/website-team/log-event.py, called by run.sh and execute.sh only
activity_log.$comment: ★ Agents never write this. An observability layer an agent can write is one it can lie to, so every event is emitted by the shell around the agent -- before it starts, after it returns, on each gate result. An agent cannot mark itself green. Outside both repositories on purpose: telemetry is neither knowledge (the vault) nor code (git), and committing it would bury real history under machine noise.
